idiom_name: asyncio.Queue for events + plain state object with async-generator or callback subscribers
implementation_notes: Python has no sealed unions and no framework stream, so the class hierarchy collapses into a plain object: the state is an attribute holding an immutable snapshot (frozen dataclass or enum), events arrive on an asyncio.Queue - documented as designed for async/await code and explicitly not thread-safe - and one consumer task reduces them sequentially, while the stream is an async generator over the subscriber list or a list of callbacks in synchronous code. Replay-one must be hand-written: expose .state for the current value and yield it first when a new subscriber attaches. For synchronous programs the same shape drops the queue entirely (a deque plus callbacks), which is why this is an idiomatic local idiom rather than library support.
pitfalls: asyncio queues are not thread-safe: producers on other threads must use loop.call_soon_threadsafe(queue.put_nowait, ev) or events are lost or the queue is corrupted.
An async generator has no replay - a subscriber attaching after the last emit sees nothing until the next state, so expose the current state attribute or emit it on subscribe.
A blocking call (requests, file I/O, CPU loop) inside the reducer stalls the whole event loop; run it in a thread or executor and feed the result back as an event.
If the consumer task raises, the queue silently stops being drained; restart the task or let the exception propagate so the failure surfaces.
